page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc8i.16xlarge is a compute-focused instance belonging to the high-clock-speed server family. The configuration is built on the x86_64 architecture and operates on the KVM hypervisor. Compute capacity is supplied by an Intel Xeon 6462C processor with 64 dedicated virtual CPUs clocked at 3.3 GHz. System memory totals 128 GB, yielding a 1:2 compute-to-memory density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. This resource distribution prioritizes raw processing throughput and high thread concurrency over memory-heavy caching or large in-memory databases.

The instance features no bundled local disk storage and contains zero hardware accelerators or GPUs. As a result, all storage needs rely entirely on network-attached storage solutions, which decouples data retention from the compute lifecycle but introduces dependency on storage-network latencies. To support intensive data exchange, the server provides a robust network baseline bandwidth of 64 Gbps. Network configurations must account for the absence of complimentary public IPv4 addresses, directing the instance toward private network environments or managed gateways.

From a workload perspective, the ecs.hfc8i.16xlarge delivers substantial compute power per physical footprint. It is suited for applications where execution speed is constrained by CPU frequency and core availability rather than expansive RAM footprints. Representative use cases include distributed build and compilation pipelines, multi-threaded batch transcoding, video rendering, scientific modeling, financial risk calculations, and high-tick-rate dedicated gaming servers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc8i.16xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server configured within the high-clock-speed instance family. Based on the x86_64 architecture and managed by KVM virtualization, it is powered by an Intel Xeon 6462C processor delivering 64 dedicated virtual cores operating at a base frequency of 3.3 GHz. Memory capacity is provisioned at 128 GB, establishing a 2 GB per core ratio aligned with compute-heavy environments. The instance includes no integrated local storage and no dedicated GPU accelerators, requiring network-attached storage volumes for persistent data. Network throughput is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 64 Gbps, facilitating high-speed data transfer across cloud services. With zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, the server is architected primarily for private VPC deployment. The hardware balance targets computational workloads requiring substantial thread capacity and high per-core clock rates, such as distributed compilation, scientific simulations, multiplayer game servers, and parallel batch processing jobs.
